title: Prior Authorization on Laboratory Test Orders
content:
## When prior authorization is required

Prior authorization is required for a Laboratory Test Orders accession when the order is billed to insurance and the class's flag for the payer class of the coverage is set:

| Payer class of the coverage billed | Flag of the class that decides |
|---|---|
| Commercial In-Network Plan, Commercial Out-of-Network Plan | prior authorization required for commercial plans |
| Medicare Advantage Plan | prior authorization (organization determination) required for Medicare Advantage plans |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan | prior authorization required for Medicaid managed care plans |
| TRICARE Prime and Select | prior authorization required for TRICARE |
| Original Medicare Part B, Medicare Supplement Plan | never required |

## Who obtains it and what is recorded

Prior authorization is requested from the payer by the ordering provider. The laboratory records the payer's decision and the authorization number only as supplied by the provider's office or by the payer, never as stated by the patient.

## Effect of the decision

- An **approved** authorization releases a testing hold placed for prior authorization pending.
- A **denied** authorization leaves the order on hold. The patient may switch the order to self-pay or cancel it. If the patient does neither, the testing hold expires under the hold rule.

## Points of judgement

- **A patient reads out an approval number from a letter.** The number is not recorded from the patient's statement. It is recorded only as supplied by the provider's office or the payer.
- **The coverage is Medicare Supplement Plan.** Prior authorization is never required for that payer class, whatever the service class.
